tasks.short: Observe officers on the units, address unprofessional behaviour, record observations in the officer's file, and discuss patterns with the manager.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor monitors behaviour of officers toward inmates, colleagues and visitors
Correctional supervisor addresses unprofessional behaviour with the officer
Correctional supervisor writes a note of observations and conversations for the officer's file
Correctional supervisor discusses patterns of behaviour with the manager

tasks.design: Observations and conversations are recorded on a short form in the HR system ({HCM}) with the type of behaviour from a list and a free note, instead of a typed note, and earlier notes show on the same file. Observing officers, addressing them and discussing patterns stay with the supervisor; no system scores officers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed later or kept in a personal notebook.
tasks.enabler_now: HR systems take short forms per employee.
tasks.still_hard: Notes must stay factual to hold up in a dispute.
tasks.human_edge: Correcting an officer without undermining them in front of inmates.

evidence.claim: HR systems can take short structured notes per employee.
Staff decisions may not rest solely on automated processing.
Systems that can monitor staff behaviour need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift underway to patterns discussed; formal discipline is outside.
Input contract: form set up in the HR system; fallback is a typed note.

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor keeps notes factual for officers to read.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a calm unit with few issues; high: a large unit with many new officers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect officers' incident and shift reports, check them, compile the daily shift report, decide follow-up, check the report, send it to management, and file the forms.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor collects incident and shift reports from officers by e-mail and paper
Correctional supervisor supervises the preparation of records by checking officers' reports and returning gaps
Correctional supervisor compiles the daily shift report in a template
Correctional supervisor decides follow-up on incidents
Correctional supervisor checks the final shift report
Correctional supervisor e-mails the shift report to management
Correctional supervisor files forms and reports on the shared drive

tasks.design: Officers fill structured incident and shift forms in the institution's records app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with required fields, so reports are not collected from the mailbox and paper and fewer come back with gaps; forms are stored there instead of filed by hand. The shift report template fills occupancy, incidents and open follow-ups from the records, and the supervisor writes the narrative and decides follow-up. No model drafts reports. Once checked, the shift report goes to management from the app.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports came by e-mail and paper and the shift report was assembled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records apps with structured forms and report templates.
tasks.still_hard: Incident narratives still need careful writing.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which incident needs follow-up tonight.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor decides follow-up instead of assembling reports.

reach.learn: Whether shift reports arrive on time.

evidence.claim: The Anchorage Police Department ended a three-month trial of AI-drafted reports because reviewing drafts ate the time saved.
Records on detainees are personal data and partly special category; access is limited by role.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift ended to forms filed; court reports are outside.
Input contract: officers use the forms; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Officers fill forms in about the time writing reports took.
The supervisor checks every shift report.
research_questions: Do reports returned for gaps fall?

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor keeps form fields and the template current.

approvals.approved_version: The shift report as checked by the supervisor in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small unit with few incidents; high: a large institution with many reports per shift.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the search or tour and pick officers, brief them, supervise the activity, and write the search report.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor plans the search or tour and checks which trained officers are on duty
Correctional supervisor briefs officers on the activity
Correctional supervisor supervises searches, shakedowns, riot control or institutional tours
Correctional supervisor writes the search report with items found

tasks.design: The duty roster ({OTHER}) shows which officers on duty are trained for searches or riot control, so the supervisor does not check training lists by hand. Searches are reported on a structured form in the records app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with cell, officers, items found and photos, instead of a typed report. Briefing and supervising the activity stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training lists were checked by hand and search reports typed afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Rostering systems hold qualifications; records apps take structured search forms.
tasks.still_hard: Riot situations leave no time for forms until afterwards.

evidence.claim: ORTEC Workforce generates schedules with labour law and collective agreements as constraints; planners keep final control.
No crime-risk prediction based solely on profiling is used.

assumptions: Boundary: from the search ordered to the search reported; criminal investigations are outside.
Input contract: qualifications kept in the roster; fallback is training lists.
research_questions: Are contraband finds recorded more completely?

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor checks qualifications in the roster are current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few planned searches; high: weekly unit searches with many items.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check who is on duty and call about absentees, conduct the roll call and briefing, assign posts, and record attendance and posts.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor checks who is on duty against the roster and phones absent officers
Correctional supervisor conducts roll calls of correctional officers with the shift briefing
Correctional supervisor assigns officers to posts
Correctional supervisor records attendance and post assignments on the roll call sheet

tasks.design: The rostering system ({OTHER}) shows sick reports and shift swaps as they happen and flags officers who are scheduled but not reported, so the supervisor phones only those. Attendance and post assignments are confirmed on the roster screen at roll call instead of written on a sheet. Conducting the roll call and assigning posts stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance was checked against a printed roster and written on a sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Rostering systems show sick reports and swaps live.
tasks.still_hard: Late arrivals still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Putting the right officer on a tense unit.

evidence.claim: ORTEC Workforce generates schedules with labour law and collective agreements as hard and soft constraints.
Working-time rules and staff monitoring need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to the roll call recorded; long-term planning is outside.
Input contract: sick reports entered in the roster; fallback is the printed roster.
Roll call briefings do not get shorter.

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor corrects attendance entered late.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small shift with stable staffing; high: a large shift with many swaps and sick reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The correctional supervisor keeps observing officers, deciding follow-up, leading searches and running roll calls; typed notes, collected reports, hand-built shift reports and roll call sheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time on the units.
